review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for simp attributes and for how USet, shell and mulHaar are used. The file has no @[simp] lemmas at all. Its new definitions (USet, shell, mulHaar) have no membership or unfolding lemmas. I did not check how other files use these definitions, and I did not run Lean. The findings are about missing interface lemmas and attributes. They are not claims of observed simp failures.

findings.excerpt: def USet : Set (v.adicCompletion K)ˣ := {u : (v.adicCompletion K)ˣ | Valued.v (u : (v.adicCompletion K)) = 1}
findings.problem: USet and shell are plain defs with no membership characterisation lemmas. Every consumer has to unfold the def by hand. `shell_zero` uses `simp [shell, USet]`. `pairwise_disjoint_shell` uses `simp only [shell, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hym hyn`. `preimage_shell` and `preimage_mul_left_shell` unfold `shell` and `USet` inside `simp only`. The main theorem then re-proves `y ∈ U ↔ Valued.v y = 1` as a local `hUmem` by `Iff.rfl` and rewrites with it manually. Unfolding these defs in simp sets leaks the `setOf` form, so downstream goals depend on the definition's internals. There is also no canonical normal form for `shell v 0` versus `USet v`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_USet {u} : u ∈ USet v ↔ Valued.v (u : v.adicCompletion K) = 1 := Iff.rfl` and `@[simp] theorem mem_shell {n y} : y ∈ shell v n ↔ Valued.v (y : v.adicCompletion K) = WithZero.exp (-n) := Iff.rfl`. Consider `@[simp] shell_zero`, oriented `shell v 0 = USet v` as it is now. The two membership lemmas are non-looping and their left sides are definitionally the right-hand predicates. Use them in `shell_zero`, `pairwise_disjoint_shell`, `preimage_shell` and `preimage_mul_left_shell` (replacing `simp only [shell, USet, ...]`). Use them in `solution` instead of the local `hUmem`.
findings.benefit: The definitions stay opaque for simp users, and membership has a single canonical rewrite. The repeated unfold-and-setOf boilerplate and the ad hoc `hUmem` in `solution` (used in `rw [hUmem]`, `(hUmem y).mpr` and `.mp`) go away.

evidence.excerpt: have hUmem : ∀ y : (p.adicCompletion ℚ)ˣ, y ∈ U ↔ Valued.v (y : p.adicCompletion ℚ) = 1 := fun y => Iff.rfl
simp only [shell, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hym hyn

findings.excerpt: have hmodU : ∀ y : (p.adicCompletion ℚ)ˣ, Valued.v (y : p.adicCompletion ℚ) = 1 →
findings.problem: The file proves `modulus_of_valued` and `modulus_shell` for general exponents. It has no simp-usable special case for valuation 1, i.e. the units of the integers. `solution` re-derives the case by hand as a local `hmodU`: it instantiates `modulus_of_valued` at `m := 0`, rewrites `zpow_zero`, and finishes with `simp`. It then rewrites with `hmodU y hy` in both `hI₁` and `hI₂`. `modulus_shell` has the shape `modulus y = absNorm ^ (-n)` under a hypothesis `y ∈ shell v n`. `n = 0` leaves `-0` and `zpow` terms that simp has to normalise each time.
findings.proposed_change: State a named lemma `modulus_eq_one_of_valued_eq_one (h : Valued.v x = 1) : modulus x = 1`, plus a simp-normal `modulus_USet`/`modulus_of_mem_USet` form of the cast to ℂ. Prove it from `modulus_of_valued v (m := 0)` with `WithZero.exp_zero` and `zpow_zero`. Tag it `@[simp]` only if the hypothesis is dischargeable by `mem_USet`. Otherwise use it as an explicit `simp [modulus_eq_one_of_valued_eq_one v hy]` argument. Replace the local `hmodU`.
findings.benefit: The factor `modulus y ^ (s - 1/2)` collapses to 1 on the unit shell by one reusable lemma. This avoids duplicated `rw [hmodU y hy, Complex.one_cpow, ...]` chains in `hI₁` and `hI₂`. It also removes the dependence on `zpow_zero` and `-0` normalisation inside the theorem body.

evidence.excerpt: rw [hmodU y hy, Complex.one_cpow, mul_one, inv_mul_cancel₀ (Units.ne_zero _)]

findings.excerpt: def mulHaar : Measure (v.adicCompletion K)ˣ := Measure.comap Units.val (mulMeasure μ)
findings.problem: `mulHaar` is a def that is only an abbreviation for `Measure.comap Units.val (mulMeasure μ)`. It has no unfolding lemma (`mulHaar_def`, or an `abbrev`). The only link between the two forms is a rfl-proved local `hμx` in `solution`. The theorem statement is written with the raw `Measure.comap ...` form, while the library lemmas (`setIntegral_shell_eq`, `integrableOn_shell_iff`, `mulHaar_USet_lt_top`) are stated for `mulHaar`. So simp and rw cannot match the two forms. `solution` needs `rw [hμx]` to transfer instances and finiteness, and it states `hHaar` separately.
findings.proposed_change: Make it an `abbrev`, or add `theorem mulHaar_def : mulHaar v μ = Measure.comap Units.val (mulMeasure μ) := rfl`. Use it so that `solution` can drop `hμx` and rewrite or simp directly. Do not tag `mulHaar_def` as simp unless the raw comap form is the intended normal form. If `mulHaar` is the preferred normal form, add the reverse-direction lemma and use it to normalise the raw comap form to `mulHaar`. Do not add both as simp lemmas, since that would loop.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical measure expression. `solution` no longer needs the ad hoc `hμx` bridge or the `rw [hμx]` steps for Haar-ness and finiteness. Lemmas about the shell integrals apply without defeq-only conversions.
